title: Day and Night: Conversations With Sapphic Desire
creator: Rebekah Cranes
description: A translation collection of the ancient Greek lyric poets — Sappho foremost, with Alcman, Anacreon, Simonides, Corinna, Hipponax, and the Roman Catullus — arranged in five movements from dawn to midnight, tracing desire from its dawn to its extinction in death. An earlier draft won the Platsis Prize for Work on the Greek Legacy (University of Michigan); first published by New Human Press, 2013. The Brief Preface argues, through Benjamin, that the untranslatable is the only element that will make it across the desert of translation. This record carries the authorial typographic form: lineation, indentation clusters, stanza and section grouping recovered from the source document 2026-08-04 (source .docx attached; recovery provenance in body_status).

The work is classified under the GENERATIVE semantic family within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. It was removed from Zenodo on June 19, 2026 and is preserved through Alexanarch.
